case_title: Santosh Moolya And Anr. v. State Of Karnataka
aggravating_circumstances: Threats to victims, illiteracy and fear
neutral_facts: The accused, two men working in a quarry, raped two sisters who were also working in the same quarry. After the rape, the accused threatened the victims that they would kill them if they informed anyone about the incident. The victims informed their mother and a coworker about the incident, but did not immediately file a police complaint due to fear and illiteracy. They finally lodged a complaint 42 days after the incident. The victims were examined by a medical officer and the accused were arrested. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 376 and 506 of the IPC, and the High Court affirmed the conviction. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction, noting that the victims' statements were reliable and that the delay in reporting the incident was due to their fear and lack of education.
